items.title: ‘Naanu Gauri’: Remembering Gauri Lankesh through a debate on campus dissent
items.summary: Nine years after an assassin tried to silence journalist Gauri Lankesh, the All India Students' Association (AISA), the student wing of the CPI(ML) Liberation, held a panel discussion titled ‘Campuses to Streets: Is Democracy Under Siege?’ in Bengaluru on September 5, marking the 9th anniversary of the journalist-activist’s assassination. Nine years after her killing, the case continues at what critics have described as a painfully slow pace. The organisers opened the event with the call “Naanu Gauri”, meaning “I am Gauri”, urging people not simply to grieve her death but to carry forward the memories and ideas she stood for. The panel featured Jawaharlal Nehru University Students' Union (JNUSU) Joint Secretary and AISA leader Danish Ali, who has been active in student politics since 2019 and was among the hunger strikers at Jantar Mantar; sociologist and author Lakshmipathi CG, who writes extensively on caste; and writer-activist Meena Kandasamy, known for her poetry on Dalit and feminist resistance. items.title: Delhi court sends Swatantra Bhardwaj to judicial custody for a day in Jantar Mantar assault case

Duty Magistrate Anjali Singh of the Patiala House Court passed the order. According to a lawyer involved in the case, Bhardwaj was produced at the judge's residence through virtual conference (VC). Police asked him to be sent to JC for 14 days. However, since he was produced before the Duty Magistrate, Bhardwaj was sent to JC for a day. The request for additional custody will be decided by the concerned court on Monday. Bhardwaj was arrested from Uttar Pradesh yesterday. He has been booked for offence of assault and provisions under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act [SC/ST Act] and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act). Bhardwaj was initially booked only for the offences under Sections 115(2) (causing simple hurt) and 126(2) (wrongful restraint) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). items.title: ‘I was shocked’: Justice RV Raveendran disagrees with Justice Nariman on full appeal against arbitral awards
items.summary: Former Supreme Court judge Justice RV Raveendran on Sunday disagreed with Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman’s recent suggestion for a full-fledged first appeal against domestic arbitral awards on facts and law, saying such a remedy would defeat the very purpose of arbitration. Justice Raveendran said he was “shocked” by the suggestion, though he acknowledged that it reflected the frustration caused by the present state of challenges to arbitral awards. “ Imagine, out of desperation, Justice Nariman said, let us have a first one appeal, full appeal and be done with it. I was shocked. But see, that is the amount of desperation .” He added, “ If you have a first appeal, then why have an arbitration? The entire purpose of arbitration is to have finality .” Justice RV Raveendran Justice Raveendran said that if courts were given wider appellate powers, including the ability to extensively reconsider or modify awards, the distinction between arbitration and ordinary litigation would begin to disappear. items.summary: The 18th edition of the SILF Turf Cricket League will begin from October 2, 2026, at Delhi. Matches will be played on weekends at the Modern School, Barakhamba Road and the Sri Guru Gobind Singh College of Commerce, Pitampura. All matches of the tournament will be live-streamed on YouTube with commentary and scorecards. There will also be facilities of 3rd Umpire for run-out and stumping decisions at all matches played at Modern School. The registration deadline for the event falls on September 14, 2026 . Each team will play a minimum of three league games and one knockout game as part of the tournament. Customised coloured clothes, including t-shirts, lowers, pullovers, and caps, will be given to the 15-member squads of the teams. From this edition onwards, the Man of the Tournament Trophy will be named after Late Arun Jaitley, recognising his contribution to public life and the legal fraternity. Dr. Lalit Bhasin , President of SILF, will host the Captains for the draw of lots in the last week of September.
